interpretation: Exact-point Thalassia re-recording after a one-year loss is substantially more fragile than uninterrupted occupancy at the next annual observation. This supports a hysteresis/incomplete-recovery pattern at the observation-state level: presence can return before local state stability is restored.
ecological_synthesis: Recovery of the coarse recorded state is not equivalent to recovery of local stability. Combined with state decoupling, community insurance, and focal-specific local history, Tampa supports a multi-state resilience model in which occupancy loss and reappearance can occur on a more fragile trajectory than long-term continuous occupancy.
next_hypothesis: Test whether pre-loss local abundance/condition predicts which returned meter marks remain stable versus re-lose, distinguishing shallow reappearance from deeper state recovery.
claim_boundary: Recorded re-loss is an observation-state transition, not demographic relapse, mortality, or failed recolonization.
The result is adjusted for stable node and return year but is not an experimental matched-control design.
Fragility may reflect patchiness, detectability, residual stress, or demographic instability.
Do not describe re-recording as full ecological recovery.
